text.p: Cosmos Bottling Corp, the beverage unit of diversified food company RFM Corp, has set a 1.5 billion-peso capital budget this year, up from 1.2 billion pesos last year, company officials said on Wednesday.
"We will do another good year," Cosmos executive vice president and chief operating officer Antonio Panajon told a meeting of analysts.

"We would like to continue reinforcing the strong momentum in sales growth by providing the infrastructure needed to meet the substantial unserved demand for Sunkist and Pop Cola - more bottling equipment, bottles, shell and a refurbished fleet of trucks," he said.
Sunkist and Pop Cola are two of the company's top-selling soft drinks.
Officials said the capital expenditure this year would be financed mainly by the issue of 1.5 billion pesos worth of convertible preferred shares.

The additional capital would help support the company's targets for this year. It is aiming for a 55 percent growth in net profits to 480 million pesos and sales of 3.6 billion pesos based on a volume growth of 68 percent for all its products including the Sarsi, Pop Cola, Jaz and RC Cola softdrinks line, the company said.
Cosmos expects to increase its market share in the soft drinks industry nationwide to 15 to 16 percent this year from 11 percent at the end of 1996, Panajon said.
It is particularly expanding its operations in Davao, southern Philippines and in the northern part of the country, officials said.

Due to the offering of the convertible preferred shares this year, the company said it had requested approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission to increase its authorised capital stock to 1.525 billion pesos from 1.0 billion pesos.
